\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\footnotesize
\textit{Notes:} $\checkmark$ / $\times$: modality available / unavailable; $\circ$: averaged over the six missing-modality patterns of Table~\ref{tab:missing_robustness}. Rows marked $^\dagger$ are quoted from PRIME Table~II (5-fold cross-validation test results on PRIME's own cohort splits); they were not rerun on our splits. Rows marked \texttt{I07} Test are models of this study evaluated on the held-out test folds of our 5-fold split, as recorded in their result ledger (per-cohort SD: population SD over folds): in Group~1, separately trained single-modality models; in Group~2, the frozen tri-modal PS3-style backbone. The \texttt{I07} Val $D_0$ row and Group~3 are computed on the validation folds of the same split (per-cohort SD: sample SD over folds). With all three modalities present, TriModalSurv applies the complete-modality identity bypass $D_0$ and returns the backbone prediction unchanged, so the bypass rows are not credited to TriModalSurv and are not bolded. Avg.: SD is the sample SD across the five cohort means. Bold: best value per column within Group~3. Hyperparameter protocol: Ours (\texttt{M6-a}) uses hyperparameters selected on the validation folds, and the same validation folds are used for reporting, so its numbers are optimistic relative to the other rows; every other row uses fixed default hyperparameters (\texttt{@default}) or has no hyperparameter grid.
\end{minipage}
